issue.title: FUSE: Transfer speed with crypt while using seek and nginx

repository.name: rclone
repository.description: "rsync for cloud storage" - Google Drive, S3, Dropbox, Backblaze B2, One Drive, Swift, Hubic, Wasabi, Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob, Azure Files, Yandex Files

issue.body:
This issues seems to mostly be a repeat of #774 which appears to be fixed in some scenarios but not all. 

I have an encrypted mounted amazon cloud drive share which is available in nginx [as a directory listing] and have found the speed issue still exists here. File copies are between 100-400Kb/s where as copies from bash run at full speed.

Strangely, I can use other applications such as SCP and get full speed with this [where as I didn't pre v1.33-69-gd8d1102]. Other comments in that issue appear to suggest it has been fixed in other applications too. 

Is this something unique with the way nginx uses seek?

issue.title: Encrypted ACD: ReadFileHandle.Read error: failed to authenticate decrypted block - bad password?

repository.name: rclone
repository.description: "rsync for cloud storage" - Google Drive, S3, Dropbox, Backblaze B2, One Drive, Swift, Hubic, Wasabi, Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob, Azure Files, Yandex Files

issue.body:
I keep getting the below error message with Encrypted Amazon Cloud Drive - I don't get it with Encrpyted Google when doing the exact same thing (just trying to access files from the mount - sometimes remotely). It will show up 4 times and won't open the file:

`File/Path/TEST.mkv: ReadFileHandle.Read error: failed to authenticate decrypted block - bad password?`

Ubuntu 14.04 x64
"v1.33-69-gd8d1102β"
rclone mount EACD: /path/to/mount/ --allow-other &

body:
How exactly did you cause the crash?  Were you playing a video?  If so with which player?

Can you reliably cause this crash?  If so can you post the whole log please?

Note to self: the crash was caused by the reader being nil in crypt.Decrypter.Read. How did it get to be nil is the question?  Perhaps a race between Read and Seek.

I am having the same issue. I am using the latest version of rclone from github. I mount rclone and unionfs using the same flags and options as OP just different directories. I then try to play the video in plex or copy it:
`$ cp acd/test.mkv ~/`
`cp: error reading 'acd/test.mkv': Input/output error`
The file is 300MB. This errors happens reliably everytime I try to read the file from the unionfs mount. I can read the file perfectly fine directly from the rclone mount. 

logs
[rclone-errors.txt](https://github.com/ncw/rclone/files/554457/rclone-errors.txt)
[rclone-log.txt](https://github.com/ncw/rclone/files/554456/rclone-log.txt)
[rclone-erros-debug-fuse.txt](https://github.com/ncw/rclone/files/554481/rclone-erros-debug-fuse.txt)

So I'm getting these errors:
`runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference`
`ReadFileHandle.Read io.Seeker failed: failed to authenticate decrypted block - bad password?` #802 although this is for a file under 10GB, #677, 

edit: attached debug-fuse logs because of `fuse: panic in handler for Read` error

@ncw In my case, unionfs doesn't crash at all.  I do get errors with the rclone fuse mount that I can attach but it looks similar to the one above.    I can reliably recreate it with vlc or KODI.  
[out.gz](https://github.com/ncw/rclone/files/554478/out.gz)
@ncw My mistake I should have been more clear, it crashes the mediaplayer. Plex in this case. I even tried AUFS and the more native OverlayFS. Same problem.
Does anybody have a workaround in the mean time?

Thanks for the logs.

Examining them closely I can see that reads are being issued from mutiple threads simultaneously.  Which lead me to a bit of missing locking in the FUSE module.

Here is a beta with the fix - let me know if it works: http://beta.rclone.org/v1.33-83-g8710741/ (will be uploaded in 15-30 mins)
Confirmed fixed the issue unionfs works now! Thanks for the speedy fix can close this issue off :)
@calisro does that fix your issue too?
@ncw Sure does.  I verified with unionfs and then also verified its working through my nginx setup down through unionfs.  Thanks.
Excellent - I'm going to close this now
